analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Vision is a genuine East India consumption story riding the underpenetrated Bihar/Jharkhand market with impressive 36% revenue CAGR and 30% ROCE — the kind of regional-to-national retail rollout I love. However, at 61x P/E with razor-thin 6.57% operating margins, deteriorating free cash flow (₹-78 Cr in FY25), and rising debt (₹480 Cr), the market has already priced in perfection with no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Exceptional growth engine: Revenue ₹899 Cr → ₹2,260 Cr in 3 years (36% CAGR) with Net Profit CAGR of 44.1% — proven execution in underpenetrated East India market
ROCE of 29.95% is genuinely impressive for electronics retail, indicating disciplined capital deployment despite asset-light expansion
Strong institutional validation: FII 16.18% + DII 19.57% = ~36% combined, suggesting credible growth thesis accepted by smart money
key_risks: Worsening free cash flow crisis: FCF turned deeply negative (-₹78 Cr FY25 vs. -₹41 Cr FY24) despite strong profit growth — a structural working capital trap common in inventory-heavy electronics retail
Valuation pricing in a decade of perfection: 61x P/E and 36.6x EV/EBITDA on a 6.57% operating margin business leaves zero buffer for any execution miss or demand slowdown

Debt trajectory is alarming: Total debt nearly doubled from ₹282 Cr (FY22) to ₹480 Cr (FY25), and D/E of 0.65 exceeds my comfort zone — financing growth with debt while burning operating cash is unsustainable
red_flags: Operating Cash Flow negative two consecutive years (FY24: -₹6 Cr, FY25: -₹41 Cr) — profits are not converting to cash, raising inventory/receivables quality questions
Promoter holding at 47.14% is below my 50% threshold — any further dilution signals lack of conviction or need for distress capital
Finance costs rising (₹25→₹39 Cr over 3 years) while business burns cash — leverage cycle could accelerate if consumer durables demand softens
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aditya Vision is exactly the kind of India consumption story that gets my pulse racing — a regional electronics retailer methodically expanding across Bihar, Jharkhand, and Eastern India, markets that national chains like Croma and Reliance Digital have historically neglected. The 36% revenue CAGR over three years and a ROCE of nearly 30% tell me the unit economics work and management can deploy capital efficiently. This is a real business serving real demand from a rising aspirational middle class in one of India's most populous and underserved geographies.

However, the financial plumbing is telling me a different story. A business reporting ₹106 Cr net profit yet burning ₹41 Cr in operating cash flow (and ₹78 Cr in FCF) is a business with a structural working capital problem — likely from bulging inventory and extended supplier cycles that will worsen as they scale faster. Funding this growth with debt (up 70% to ₹480 Cr in three years) while cash generation deteriorates is a dangerous combination. At 61x trailing P/E for a 6.57% operating margin retailer, I am being asked to pay a luxury goods valuation for a commodity distribution business. I would revisit this at 25-30x P/E with demonstrable FCF improvement — perhaps around ₹200-220 per share — but at ₹523, the risk-reward is firmly against me.
